papers.title: Protocol-aware dual-view single-channel EEG sleep staging with improved N1 discrimination on public sleep-EDF and SHHS benchmarks.
papers.summary: Developed DualViewSeqSleepNet, a protocol-aware single-channel EEG sleep-staging model combining waveform and spectral encoders with cross-epoch aggregation and N1-aware supervision. On Sleep-EDF it reached macro-F1 0.821 and accuracy 0.869, raising N1 F1 from 0.506 to 0.535, and achieved macro-F1 0.791 on SHHS-1 without retuning.

papers.title: Enabling Rapid Calibration of BCI Systems that Detect Movement-Related Cortical Potentials in Children with Cerebral Palsy.
papers.summary: Developed a Bi-LSTM deep-learning framework for detecting movement-related cortical potentials during ankle dorsiflexion in four children with cerebral palsy across 27 EEG sessions. Cross-subject cumulative learning reached 91% accuracy without within-session calibration, and adding transfer learning raised accuracy to 93% with minimal calibration, outperforming conventional strategies.

papers.title: Childhood and adolescent changes in sleep spindle trends across the night.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: Detected and measured sleep spindles across 1,944 nights from 97 participants aged 6-18 to characterize cycle trends in spindle density, frequency, amplitude, and duration and their relation to delta EEG trends. Spindle density and duration increased steeply between early cycles, with age-related reductions in these trends and shifts in frequency/amplitude trends indicating maturation of thalamocortical and frontal circuits beyond simple pruning.

papers.title: High-Density EEG Signatures of Cataplexy in Narcolepsy Type 1.
papers.summary: Used 128-channel EEG polysomnography in 10 drug-free adults with narcolepsy type 1 to characterize the electrophysiological signature of 73 cataplexy epochs versus wake, N1, and REM states. Cataplexy showed a distinct hybrid EEG profile with intermediate sleep-wake spectral features and mixed wake/REM/N1 hypnodensity probabilities, differing from direct-entry REM sleep.

papers.title: Periodic generalized nonepileptiform discharges (PGNDs) during NREM sleep before nocturnal seizures in temporal and extratemporal lobe epilepsy: An exploratory quantitative EEG study.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed preictal periodic generalized nonepileptiform discharges (PGNDs) in 68 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients (35 TLE, 33 ETLE) with quantitative EEG. Relative delta power of the PGND just before nocturnal seizure onset was higher in ETLE than TLE (51.6% vs 45.1%), suggesting localization-related differences rather than a preictal biomarker.

papers.title: Hidden Drowsiness in Wakefulness: Differences in Resting-State EEG Profiles in Natural Short Sleepers Versus Recommended Length Sleepers.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state eyes-open EEG in natural short sleepers versus recommended-length sleepers, finding higher global alpha power and regionally steeper aperiodic exponents (especially occipital) in natural short sleepers, both markers of increased drowsiness. A Group × Region interaction and a trend toward increasing aperiodic exponents over time suggested less stable wakefulness under low stimulation.

papers.title: Transformer-based EEG source imaging localizes pathological high-frequency oscillations in focal epilepsy.
papers.summary: Introduced TH-DeepSIF, a transformer-based deep source-imaging framework trained on neural mass model simulations to localize high-frequency oscillations from scalp EEG. In 20 drug-resistant epilepsy patients, pathological spike-ripple sources matched resection regions with median error 10.9 mm and specificity 0.883, and were close to the seizure onset zone in a six-patient intracranial subset.

papers.title: Directional brain-heart interaction during cognitive workload: a permutation conditional mutual information approach.
papers.summary: Applied Permutation Conditional Mutual Information (PCMI) to characterize directional brain-heart interaction, first validating it on synthetic coupled time series and then on simultaneous EEG-ECG recordings during baseline and mental arithmetic in 36 subjects. Brain-heart interaction complexity increased during mental arithmetic, mainly involving anterior and posterior scalp regions and vagal- and sympathovagal-related HRV components.

papers.title: EEG biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases: Machine learning applications and clinical trial insights.
papers.summary: This review synthesized evidence from 226 studies on EEG-based biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases, mapping diagnosis, prognosis, treatment monitoring, and patient stratification. It reports spectral power, event-related potentials, and connectivity as main features, with support vector machines and neural networks as primary classifiers, while noting challenges of small samples, methodological heterogeneity, limited interpretability, and gaps in clinical validation.

papers.title: TToTP model: An automated detection of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia using Tesla Tree of Thought Pattern with EEG signals.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a self-organized explainable feature engineering model using a novel Tesla Tree of Thought Pattern (TToTP) feature extractor, cumulative weighted iterative neighborhood component analysis, tkNN classification, and iterative majority voting to detect Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls from EEG. The model achieved over 99% classification accuracy and generated a cortical channel map.

papers.title: Seizure-like behaviors in a mutant mouse with increased calpain-dependent cleavage of αII-spectrin.
papers.summary: Using heterozygous Sptan1R1098Q mice, this study examined seizure-like behaviors alongside video-EEG and gait analysis, finding ataxia, age-related increases in delta and theta power, and spike-wave discharges. Nearly all mutants showed handling-induced seizure-like motor responses without coincident cortical ictal EEG activity, demonstrating a dissociation between behavioral seizures and cortical electrographic seizures.

papers.title: Temporal dissociation across the eye-brain-muscle cascade delineates a preparation window before muscle activation in subacute stroke.
papers.summary: Recorded eye-tracking, EEG, and EMG synchronously in 30 subacute stroke survivors and 30 controls during a nine-grid reaching task, showing stepwise delays in visual engagement and muscle activation bracketing a cortical preparation window; gaze-timing features classified reaching action occurrence with AUC 0.973 and accuracy 0.918.

papers.title: Association of the 2HELPS2B Score With Impaired Recovery of Consciousness and In-Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill Patients: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This multicenter retrospective study of 33 critically ill adults with persistent impaired consciousness examined whether a 2HELPS2B score of 2 or higher was associated with failure to improve FOUR score and in-hospital mortality. High scores were associated with failure to improve FOUR score (44.4% vs 4.2%; crude RR 10.67) but not significantly with mortality, in a small unadjusted cohort.

papers.title: Social bilingual language use is associated with neural efficiency in inhibitory control: Evidence from ERPs.
papers.summary: Fifty participants completed a language and social background questionnaire and an EEG adaptive Flanker task to test how bilingual experience modulates behavioral and neural indices of conflict processing. Greater Non-English Social Use, but not overall bilingualism or home use, was associated with attenuated N100 and N200 responses without behavioral differences, suggesting experience-dependent efficiency in control recruitment.

papers.title: Comparative outcomes following virtual reality-assisted and traditional supplementary exercise programs and usual training on balance, sprint performance, and resting-state EEG in youth academy football players.
papers.summary: In a three-arm randomized study of 39 youth-academy football players, an eight-week virtual reality-assisted supplementary exercise program was associated with greater baseline-adjusted improvements in two-leg, dominant-leg, and non-dominant-leg balance than traditional supplementary exercise or usual training. A 30-m sprint difference appeared between VR and control groups without a differential pre-post trajectory, and exploratory resting-state EEG showed differences in anterior spectral power and anterior-central synchronization.

papers.title: Label-Free Live Cell Type Prediction by Integrating Raman Spectroscopy and Machine Learning.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using coherent Raman spectroscopy combined with a shallow XGBoost classifier, the authors profiled 286 live single cells from patient-derived glioma lines and distinguished IDH1-mutant from IDH1-wild-type cells (ROC-AUC 0.78) and IDH1-mutant astrocytoma from oligodendroglioma (ROC-AUC 0.81). Feature importance implicated protein amide bands, NADH, unsaturated fatty acids, heme-related modes, and lipid-rich vesicle signatures in the separations.

papers.title: Electromagnetic field theories of conscious experience: a conceptual review and reappraisal.
papers.summary: This conceptual review contrasts electromagnetic field theories of consciousness with traditional neural and functionalist accounts, arguing that the brain's endogenous EMF provides a spatially integrating substrate for phenomenal unity. It synthesizes EEG correlations, ephaptic coupling, perturbation studies, and field computation, hypothesizing that low-frequency oscillations underlie phenomenal space while localized high-frequency oscillations support experiential differentiation.

papers.title: Acupuncture and related needling in sports-related knee rehabilitation: a narrative review of neurophysiological mechanisms and assessment methods.
papers.summary: This hypothesis-generating narrative review synthesizes indirect evidence on manual acupuncture, electroacupuncture, and trigger point dry needling as adjuncts in sports-related knee rehabilitation, organizing possible mechanisms into cortical, corticospinal/spinal-reflexive, and peripheral muscular levels. It reports that direct evidence in sports knee injury populations remains limited and proposes assessment via fNIRS, EEG, TMS, and EMG.

papers.title: Lewis ladder: A web application that draws ladder diagrams from the surface electrocardiogram.
papers.summary: The authors present Lewis Ladder, a free web application that measures P-wave and QRS onsets from a surface ECG strip, applies 11 exclusion and 24 caution rules to 14 candidate readings, and draws corresponding ladder diagrams. On 28 synthetic tracings, the intended reading was never excluded even with random mark displacement up to 20 ms SD across 11,200 classifications, with 794 automated checks covering the engine.

papers.title: Seizure Freedom After Focal Epilepsy Surgery in a Child With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex and Coexisting Suspected Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report of a 3-year-old girl with tuberous sclerosis complex and drug-resistant focal epilepsy who became clinically seizure-free for 18 months after neuronavigation-guided left frontal resection, with emergence of independent walking and syllabic speech despite persistent epileptiform EEG activity.

papers.title: Projected Demand for Cardiac Electrophysiology Procedures in Australia to 2040: A National Population-Based Modelling Study.
papers.summary: A national population-based modelling study using Australian hospital procedural data from 2010-2024 projected cardiac electrophysiology procedural demand to rise 43.4% to 80,185 procedures annually by 2040, driven mainly by catheter ablation, especially atrial fibrillation ablation.

papers.title: Novel antimicrobial pyrimidin-2-one (thione) azo disperse dyes for polyester fabrics.
papers.summary: The study synthesized a series of pyrimidinone (thione) azo disperse dyes, evaluated their dyeing performance on polyester, and found compounds 4a and 4b were the most potent antimicrobial agents against multidrug-resistant S. haemolyticus, K. pneumoniae, and C. albicans, though with moderate cytotoxicity.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
